rq: joint identification of raw language equivalence and latent intervention partition
primary_work: Hanjie, Zhong, and Narasimhan, Grounding Language to Entities and Dynamics for Generalization in Reinforcement Learning, ICML 2021
decision: NARROWED BEYOND REWARD-SUFFICIENT ENTITY-AND-DYNAMICS GROUNDING — NOT ADOPTED
reason: Messenger/EMMA already learns a reward-sufficient latent alignment from free-form manuals to entity symbols and environment dynamics and demonstrates zero-shot combination generalization. However, reward, fixed action semantics, entity inventory, generator structure, and benchmark splits provide task supervision; simultaneous manual/entity/role/environment recoding preserves the complete interactive law and policy metrics; and reward-equivalent targets or policy-equivalent manuals can support different raw-language and target partitions. No joint identifiability theorem for Q, P, and denotation is established.
surviving_candidate: After recovering the finest language equivalence supported by legitimate language observations, the finest target partition supported by non-language interventions, and the strongest reward-sufficient manual-to-world alignment obtainable in Messenger-like interaction, determine whether a preregistered cross-system intervention law uniquely separates only the remaining policy- and reward-aliased classes while eliminating every manual/entity/role/environment recoding preserving the complete language, transition, reward, and action laws.
public_baseline_reproduction: not started; official environment/model code and exact commit are available, but hermetic dependencies, external-weight checksums, canonical three-seed manifest, resource protocol, artifact checksums, and direct Q/P/d metrics must be preregistered first
